text:
Priya: Thinking through a 'gradual fallback' UX that emphasizes observability + operator control. Idea: three lightweight modes - sample, shard, circuit - and a small heatmap showing where fallbacks are happening across tenants/regions.
Dan: Love the heatmap. We should include bins for error_type (5xx,timeouts,quality) and a clickable cell that opens a decision trace. Important: all fallbacks must surface an explain link that shows metric snapshot + active triggers.
Zoe: UX ideas: compact badge on rollout row (color + tiny sparkline). Click -> panel with heatmap, recent decision traces, sampled examples (hashes only by default), and two primary actions: Fast-Promote and Pause-Fallback. Fast-Promote should require justification and show estimated cost impact.
Marco: Telemetry needs: fallback_mode (sample|shard|circuit), fallback_reason_code (enum), decision_sig (stable id), sampled_bool, sample_seed, tenant_id, region. Keep each event tiny. For sampled items include prompt_hash and response_hash (sha256) only. Raw text only if customer opts in.
Priya: API shape proposal (stringified in RFC) includes fields: mode, triggers[], sample_fraction, shard_fraction, circuit_conditions, billing_policy (original|target|budget_safe), allow_fast_promote (bool), audit_retention_days. We'll RFC exact schema.
Dan: Deterministic sampling is required for replay. Use seeded hash of (seed || tenant_id || prompt_hash || request_id) mod 1e9 < fraction*1e9. Document fallback_decision_sig = hex(HMAC(seed, key)).
Zoe: Replay workflow: queue sampled decision_sig -> operator picks item -> Replay runs against both routes in sandbox with side-by-side token, latency, and a semantic diff score. Show a tiny provenance header (model id/version, hardware tier). No plaintext unless opt-in.
Marco: Operator flows: Pause-Fallback (snooze durations), Fast-Promote (promote sample->shard->circuit with cooldown), Revert. Each action creates an immutable audit event with operator id, reason, ticket link optional. Reverts and promotes should be idempotent with clear rollback paths.
Priya: Edge case: cheaper fallback model that increases latency. Add an automatic guard: if promoted_shard p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.2 for 5m, auto-revert and tag reason AUTO_REVERT_LATENCY. Also surface this in heatmap.
Dan: Billing: default to billing_policy = target. Add budget_safe mode that throttles fallback when projected spend > budget_threshold. Console should show projected delta before enabling a stage.
Zoe: Visuals: heatmap rows=tenant, cols=region, cell shows small sparkline + count. Hover shows recent reason codes. Decision trace panel shows a short stack: triggers, metric snapshots, sample_fraction, decision_sig, and quick links (replay, promote, snooze).
Marco: Telemetry versioning: add these as optional fields in telemetry v3 to keep backward compatibility. Also create a compact audit CSV export (no raw content) with columns: timestamp, rollout_id, decision_sig, mode, reason_code, tenant_id, region, action, operator.
Priya: Privacy: default to hash-only. If customer opts in for full artifacts, require explicit org-level consent and a retention policy. Deletion requires 2 admins and an audit entry.
Dan: QA: unit tests for deterministic sampling boundaries, integration tests for promote->auto-revert latency guard, and e2e for audit CSV generation and replay sandbox.
Zoe: Add a small 'why-we-fell-back' modal that presents the most actionable signal in plain english for product folks (e.g., "p95 latency increased 45% in us-east-1, error-rate climbed to 3.7% in 5m window"). Keep it concise.
Marco: Implementation note: compute sample decision at edge proxy to avoid RPCs. Emit decision_sig downstream in request headers so backend traces can correlate.
infra-bot: Feature flag created: gradual-fallback-ux -> ff-6180
deploy-bot: Canary rollout created: service/redwood-gradual-fallback -> id=canary-6180000000
Priya: I'll open the RFC with API + telemetry + mockups. Assigning @Zoe for mockups, @Marco for telemetry schema, and @Dan for sampling impl/tests. Thanks all.
